title: Legacy Embodiment Practice
opening: You can express a quality you value before you earn a title or complete a large project. Choose a suitable ordinary action, try it, then look at what it actually changed.

labels.comparison: Help someone think through one question
labels.comparisonIntro: Suppose a colleague values helping people think independently. When someone asks for help, they could supply an answer immediately or ask a useful question and leave time for the other person to reason.
labels.adherenceText: Helping people think independently can guide an ordinary conversation. A title or distant educational project is not required for every expression of that quality.
labels.valueText: For a suitable question, ask what the person has tried and what they notice. Give them room to reason and offer help where it is needed. If the situation needs preparation or direct assistance, choose that response instead.
labels.outcomeText: Look at what happened in the conversation and whether it helped the person reason. One helpful interaction can express the quality; it does not establish a whole teaching system or a lasting effect.
labels.signalQuestion: Choose a part of the comparison
labels.rhythmTitle: Choose an action that serves the situation
labels.rhythmText: An ordinary act matters through what it does for the people involved. Publicizing it does not establish its value. Some contributions need preparation before direct action is possible; a truthful preparation step is useful too. Keep the scale of the claim matched to what happened, then adjust the action if it did not serve the quality you intended.
labels.practice: Bring one valued quality into this week
labels.practiceIntro: Keep the notes that help you decide what to try or change. You can save a partial note and return after the attempt.
labels.private: This private note is optional. The six course questions remain separate.
labels.length: This full reflection is over 2,000 characters. Shorten it to save; all of your text stays here.
labels.sourceQuote:
Legacy Embodiment Practice
For a valued quality or contribution, ask how it can appear in an ordinary action this
week. Choose the action and context, do it and examine the experience. This
connects the desired life with something you can live now.

fields.label: The quality or contribution you value
An ordinary situation where it could matter
One suitable action you could take

What happened and what the action actually changed
What you would keep, change or try next

example.contribution: A colleague asks for help with a question they are able and willing to explore.
example.avoid: Ask what they have tried and what they notice, then leave room for their reasoning.
example.present: Check that the situation allows time to explore; offer direct help if it is needed.
example.change: Notice what helps the colleague reason, then adjust the amount of help in the next suitable conversation.

source.assessmentBoundary: Six required open-ended assessment questions remain separate from this optional private reflection. No qualified semantic grade or evidence of learner effectiveness is supplied.
